source.section: PDF page 14 Schedule RS instructions (Civil Service Retirement System, Social Security not reported; IRA distributions on Schedule RS); PDF page 7; Form 40 (25f40blk.pdf page 1) lines 5b to 18; booklet PDF page 8 lines 5 to 13, PDF page 10 lines 14 and 17; PDF page 9 Standard Deduction chart (line 11, PDF page 8); Form 40 page 1 boxes 1 to 4 (personal exemption, line 13); tax table PDF pages 25 to 30

worked: Federal AGI = federal Civil Service Retirement System pension 40,000.00 + IRA distribution (person 0) 20,000.00 + taxable Social Security 20,400.00 + interest 2,000.00 = 82,400.00. Federal taxable income = 82,400.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65 additional = 64,650.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Alabama: the projection starts from federal AGI and removes exempt income (Form 40 builds its own lines 5b to 10, which give the same AGI for this household). Subtract federal Civil Service Retirement System pension 40,000.00: Civil Service Retirement System and United States Retirement System benefits are not reported (PDF page 14 Schedule RS list; PDF page 7). Subtract taxable Social Security 20,400.00: Social Security is exempt (PDF page 7 'Federal Social Security benefits'; PDF page 14); never reported on Form 40. IRA distribution 20,000.00 stays in: taxable, reported on Schedule RS (PDF page 14), Form 40 page 2 Part I line 4 to line 7. Interest 2,000.00 stays in: bank interest is taxable, Form 40 line 6. Form 40 line 10 Alabama AGI = 22,000.00. Line 11 standard deduction (single, chart PDF page 9): AL AGI 22,000.00 is in the first band (0 to 25,999.00), the full amount, so 3,000.00. Line 12 federal income tax deduction: the form subtracts the 2025 federal income tax (worksheet PDF page 31); the projection does not model it (not_modelled, approximation), so 0.00 here. Line 13 personal exemption (single) 1,500.00. Line 14 dependent exemption 0.00 (no dependents). Line 15 total deductions = 3,000.00 + 0.00 + 1,500.00 + 0.00 = 4,500.00. Line 16 taxable income = 22,000.00 - 4,500.00 = 17,500.00. Line 17 tax from the derived single / married filing separately / head of family schedule (2% from 0, 4% from 500, 5% from 3,000): (500.00 - 0.00) x 0.02 = 10.00 + (3,000.00 - 500.00) x 0.04 = 100.00 + (17,500.00 - 3,000.00) x 0.05 = 725.00 = 835.00; the tax table row 17,500-17,600 (single / married filing separately / head of family column, PDF pages 25 to 30) gives 838. Line 18 net tax due, no credits: 835.00. Federal taxable Social Security: provisional income 40,000.00 + 20,000.00 + 2,000.00 + 12,000.00 = 74,000.00; 0.85 x (74,000.00 - 34,000.00) + 4,500.00 = 38,500.00, capped at 0.85 x 24,000.00 = 20,400.00 (given).
accepted_approximations: The federal income tax deduction is not applied (not_modelled).

The brackets are derived from the tax table. Under 100,000 the table taxes each 100-dollar row at its midpoint, rounded; above 100,000 the printed worksheet ((income - 100,000) x .05 + 4,958, or + 4,918 joint) is 2 dollars below the derived brackets.
